summary: Stores two integer payload values into the progress-bar ring buffer. Reads the current write pointer from dword_8AAE64, optionally bumps the ring-buffer count dword_83EE60 (guard < 1023) and advances the pointer by 432 bytes, loads the session time float dbl_8AFEA0, then encodes a progress bar event via ProgressBarEventEncode (4, 21, 8, 255, time, 1) and writes a1 to buffer[2] and a2 to buffer[3] relative to the write pointer. Returns a1. Invoked by sub_4D4580 (004D4580).

local_names.a1: first payload value, stored at buffer index 2 and returned
local_names.a2: second payload value, stored at buffer index 3
local_names.v2: ring buffer write pointer loaded from dword_8AAE64
local_names.v4: session time float loaded from dbl_8AFEA0
local_names.result: echo of a1 returned to the caller

operations.description: Loads the current ring buffer write pointer from dword_8AAE64 into local v2
When the ring buffer count dword_83EE60 is below 1023, increments the count and advances the write pointer dword_8AAE64 by 432 bytes; otherwise the pointer stays put
Loads the current session time as a float from dbl_8AFEA0 into local v4
ProgressBarEventEncode(v2, 4, 21, 8, 255, v4, 1) encodes a progress bar event (type 21, subtype 8, colour/intensity 255, timestamp v4) into the ring buffer at the write pointer
Writes a1 to buffer index 2 and a2 to buffer index 3 relative to the write pointer v2
Returns a1, echoing the first argument back to the caller
Invoked by sub_4D4580 (004D4580), the only known caller

unresolved: Ring buffer entries are written even when the capacity guard (count < 1023) fails; the event and payload land at the current pointer regardless of whether the counter was bumped
